title: Multi-model shadow-to-canary transition race and safety-gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a rollout that converted multiple shadowed baseline models into active canaries, a race between the shadow-merge controller and the variant routing reconciler caused transient duplicate canary assignments across different shards. That duplication amplified request fanout for several multi-model routes, overloading dedicated pools and causing KV cache divergence and two failed automated rollbacks. The incident increased tail latency, produced elevated error rates for a subset of enterprise customers, and required a manual rollback to a pinned version. This ticket captures the postmortem findings and action items to harden the shadow->canary transition path and rollback safety gates.
timeline: 2025-02-18 03:07 UTC - Canary rollout job started for multi-model routing group 'mm-group-7' (orchestrator triggered by release runtime-1.19).
2025-02-18 03:09 UTC - Shadow-merge controller issued merge that marked two models as eligible for canary simultaneously due to parallel reconcile loop.
2025-02-18 03:12 UTC - Router reconciler applied assignments; two canary variants were active in overlapping shards leading to 2x request duplication for ~15% of traffic to mm-group-7.
2025-02-18 03:15 UTC - Dedicated GPU pools for mm-group-7 reached sustained CPU/GPU bound utilization and began shedding requests. KV cache syncs started failing with version mismatch errors.
2025-02-18 03:18 UTC - Automated rollback attempted but rollback controller could not acquire pinlock due to version-pin race and partial shard state; rollback action failed and retried twice.
2025-02-18 03:27 UTC - SRE manual intervention: connector fencing and forced single-variant pin applied; traffic restored to baseline by 03:33 UTC.
2025-02-18 04:00 UTC - Incident declared mitigated; postmortem workstream opened.
root_causes: Race condition between shadow-merge controller and routing reconciler allowing concurrent canary eligibility marks.
Router assignment logic did not enforce a global single-candidate-per-shard invariant during reconciles.
KV cache versioning relies on eventual sync; partial duplicate assignments led to inconsistent cache keys and mismatched eviction headers.
Rollback controller pin acquisition is optimistic and lacks a backoff+quarantine path for partial shard pin failures.
No pre-deployment capacity gate for multi-model fanout; autoscaler reacted too slowly to amplified demand.
impact_summary: Affected ~15% of mm-group-7 requests for 18 minutes. Tail latency increased by 3-5x for enterprise routes; two customers reported API timeouts and one customer experienced transient 5-minute error burst. Billing impact was negligible but SLA credit discussions initiated with affected accounts.
mitigations_applied_during_incident: Manual connector fencing to isolate duplicate canary variants.
Forced pin to baseline model version across mm-group-7 shards.
Temporarily increased autoscaler reaction aggressiveness for affected pools.
Added additional monitoring alert for duplicate-variant assignments and KV version-mismatch spike.
action_items: Marcus Liu - Implement global single-candidate-per-shard check in routing reconciler + unit tests - due 2025-03-05 - estimate 5
Priya Kapoor - Add leader-election barrier to shadow-merge controller to avoid parallel eligibility marks - due 2025-03-03 - estimate 3
Jordan Reyes - Enhance rollback controller: implement backoff+quarantine path when pin acquisition partially fails, and add audit logs for pin state - due 2025-03-10 - estimate 5
SRE Team (Elena Martinez) - Create emergency playbook entry: 'forced-pin-and-fence' with exact CLI steps and verification checks - due 2025-02-28 - estimate 2
Runtime team - Introduce pre-rollout capacity gate that simulates amplified fanout for multi-model routes (dry-run) - due 2025-03-12 - estimate 8
Observability - Surface KV cache version-mismatch metric on Console per-route dashboard and add a 10m composite alert - owner: Liam Chen - due 2025-02-27 - estimate 2
QA - Add regression test that simulates concurrent shadow->canary transitions and verifies no duplicate assignments - owner: QA Automation - due 2025-03-05 - estimate 3
acceptance_criteria: Routing reconciler prevents duplicate canary assignments in unit and integration tests.
Rollback controller demonstrates successful recovery in a simulated partial-pin-failure test in CI.
Pre-rollout capacity gate exists and blocks rollouts that would exceed safe fanout thresholds unless explicitly approved, with an override audit log.
New alerting rules trigger on duplicate-variant assignment and KV version mismatch and produce an opsrun checklist.

notes: This incident highlighted a class of races that only show up for multi-model fanout patterns. Proposed longer-term work includes model-aware routing invariants and per-route dry-run gates before promotion to canary. We'll track that as a separate RFC after finishing the immediate action items.
